clue.text: Fishing boats having no particular destination?

explanation.surface: A description of trawlers wandering aimlessly at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Drifters are boats fishing with drift nets, and also people who wander aimlessly without a fixed goal.

clue.text: As ordered, spread glue — then get scolded about it

indicators.note: the scolding word goes round, enclosing the other letters

parts.note: to be rated is an old word for being scolded

indicators.note: glue that is spread is pushed about, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to apply glue, then receive a telling-off for the mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' makes EGUL from GLUE, and 'about' puts it inside RATED (scolded) after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Something regulated is controlled or arranged according to rules, as ordered.

clue.text: The Spanish set out to get him

indicators.note: the word for set lies outside, wrapping round the Spanish article

parts.note: to fix something is to set it in place
el is the Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: Spanish forces leave to capture a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' puts EL inside FIX. The definition is just 'him': the clue treats a man's name as a male person.
explanation.definitionFit: Felix is a man's name, so it can stand for a male person referred to as him.

clue.text: See ex-prince's new version of what actually happened

indicators.note: a new version of the letters means they are rearranged into fresh order

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter, leaving the letters of ex-prince

explanation.surface: An invitation to read a former royal's revised memoir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new version of' rearranges SEE plus EXPRINCE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Experiences are events lived through, the things that really occurred to someone.

clue.text: Got rid of the slugs — just about every one — found in the allotment

indicators.note: the shooting word is placed about, enclosing the word for every one

parts.note: shot the slugs, killing off the garden pests
all means every one

explanation.surface: A gardener kills nearly all the slugs on the allotment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just about' puts ALL inside SHOT after SH. The definition is loose: a vegetable grown on an allotment, a British rented garden plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small onion-like vegetable commonly grown on garden plots.

clue.text: Damson pie for 1 across

indicators.note: pie is printers' type jumbled up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fruit pie recipe offered to fishing boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pie' is the anagram indicator, from printer's pie (jumbled type). '1 across' points to DRIFTERS in its sense of wanderers.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomads have no fixed home and roam about, just as drifters do.

clue.text: Pigeon looking both ways

indicators.note: the word reads the same whichever direction you look along it

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A bird checking for traffic before crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: A nun is a breed of fancy pigeon; 'looking both ways' says the word is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: The nun is a domestic breed of fancy pigeon with a hood of feathers.

clue.text: I am in bewilderment — horses with edible ears?

indicators.note: the clue says I am in, so the letter I sits inside the next word

parts.note: a maze is a state of bewilderment
cobs are sturdy short-legged horses

explanation.surface: Someone confused by the sight of horses with ears you could eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'am in' puts I inside MAZE to make MAIZE.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn grows in ears, the seed-bearing heads that people eat.

clue.text: He wrote of French adversary

parts.note: de is French for 'of'
a foe is an adversary

explanation.surface: A writer describing a French enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: Daniel Defoe wrote Robinson Crusoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe was an English novelist, author of Robinson Crusoe.

clue.text: Shakespeare's equal?

parts.note: not a rival dramatist but the word Shakespeare used for level or even, borrowed from French

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare used this French-derived form meaning even or level in Measure for Measure.

clue.text: Ugly rows in court?

parts.note: plain can mean unattractive
tiffs are petty quarrels

explanation.surface: Unsightly quarrels breaking out in a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the cryptic 'in court?': the parties who bring cases there.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaintiffs are the people who bring a lawsuit, appearing before judges.

clue.text: Priest taking team recipe for invigorating drink

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel
XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team
R is the abbreviation for recipe (Latin recipe, 'take')

explanation.surface: A clergyman following his team's formula for a tonic.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic potion supposed to revive or prolong life.

clue.text: Hung around to see it before start of day

parts.note: lo, an old word for look or behold
ere is a poetic word for before

indicators.note: the start of the word day gives its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone waited about to watch something before dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to linger idly without purpose.

clue.text: Vessels making friendly overtures?

explanation.surface: Ships extending a welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships that clear frozen seas, and remarks or games that ease tension between strangers.

clue.text: Large insect taking step over betel nuts

indicators.note: the word for step takes in, enclosing, the rearranged letters

parts.note: a stage is a step in a process

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A big bug crossing over some betel nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' turns BETEL into BEETL, which 'taking' puts inside STAGE before its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: A large beetle whose males have antler-like jaws.

clue.text: ANile gull turning out to be a water hen

indicators.note: turning out to be suggests the letters change into something else

explanation.surface: A gull on the Nile proves to be a different waterbird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning out' rearranges A NILE GULL.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallinules are marsh birds of the rail family, such as the moorhen.

clue.text: He's unaffected by the setback

indicators.note: read backwards the name does not change, so a reversal leaves it intact

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A man who shrugs off a disappointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' is a reversal; the name reads the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a man's name, so it can stand for a male person.

clue.text: Collection of clothes that should fit the painter exactly

parts.note: something that fits to a T fits exactly
Henri Rousseau was a French painter

explanation.surface: A wardrobe tailored perfectly for an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to a T' means exactly, so T is the piece; it goes before the painter's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's outfit of clothes and linen for her marriage.

clue.text: I have old-fashioned image

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped or made, so these letters are formed anew

explanation.surface: Someone owning an outdated picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashioned' rearranges OLD into DOL; 'old-fashioned' looks like one word.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a carved figure or likeness worshipped as a god.

clue.text: Muscle required to contain newsmen between lake and river

indicators.note: the lake's name is made to contain the word for newsmen

parts.note: Como is a lake in northern Italy
the press means journalists

explanation.surface: Strength is needed to hold reporters back between water features.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to contain' puts PRESS inside COMO, before its last O; R follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A compressor is an anatomical muscle that squeezes a part of the body.

clue.text: Literature for the masses

parts.note: not popular reading, but books used by priests at Catholic services of the Mass

explanation.definitionFit: Books containing the prayers and order of service for Catholic worship.

clue.text: See slips remodelled as fur-trimmed garments

indicators.note: something remodelled is reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Petticoats altered into fur-lined coats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remodelled' rearranges SEE SLIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelisses are long cloaks or jackets lined or edged with fur.

clue.text: Duck that is turning colour

indicators.note: turning means the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
red is a colour

explanation.surface: A bird that is changing hue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses IERED.
explanation.definitionFit: Eiders are large sea ducks prized for their down.

clue.text: Ginger up a river, then another

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England, so another river

explanation.surface: Spicing up a trip from one waterway to the next.
explanation.definitionFit: To ginger up is to stimulate or excite, as is rousing someone.

clue.text: Bouquet on first grave

indicators.note: the first of the word on is its opening letter

parts.note: dour means stern or grave

explanation.surface: Flowers placed on a new grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouquet' looks floral; it is the smell of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's bouquet is its smell or aroma.

clue.text: Decide to include two girls, you'll hear

indicators.note: the phrase is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: add Judy, Kate: include two girls' names

explanation.surface: Choosing to invite a pair of young women along.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'add Judy Kate' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjudicate is to judge and settle a dispute formally.

clue.text: Reserve of diamonds

explanation.definitionFit: Ice means cold reserve of manner, and is criminal slang for diamonds.

clue.text: Concerning the above

explanation.definitionFit: Over can mean about a subject, and over also means higher than or overhead.

clue.text: Kind of block that's an easy task to move?

explanation.surface: A heavy block that is effortless to shift.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeze block is a builder's cinder block; a breeze is a cinch; to breeze is to move along briskly.

clue.text: Murmur when American twice backs luxury car on to us

indicators.note: backs means each copy is read the other way round
the word for American appears two times over

parts.note: RR is short for Rolls-Royce, the luxury car

explanation.surface: Grumbling as an American reverses a Rolls-Royce into us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' gives USUS; 'backs' reverses it to SUSU; then RR and US.
explanation.definitionFit: A susurrus is a soft whispering or rustling sound.
